title.rendered: Where the Spirit Is, There Is Freedom: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. Not coming. Not possible. Freedom is. If the Spirit lives in you, freedom is your present-tense reality.

content.rendered:
Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. Not freedom is coming. Not freedom is possible. Freedom is. And if the Spirit lives in you, freedom is your present-tense reality.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, May 30, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”
2 Corinthians 3:17 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Freedom is one of the most longed-for words in the human heart. Every age has its own bondages. Religious systems that turn devotion into performance. Cultures that quietly tell you who to be. Inner voices that whisper you are not enough, not loved enough, not free enough. And in the middle of all of that, Paul writes a single sentence that cuts every chain: where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

Look at the verb. Not where the Spirit is, freedom is possible. Not freedom is coming. Not freedom can be earned. Freedom is. Present tense. Already true. The Spirit and freedom show up together. They are not two separate gifts. Where one is, the other is.

And freedom from what? Read your New Testament and the list is long. Freedom from condemnation, because in Christ Jesus there is no condemnation (Romans 8:1). Freedom from performance, because we no longer relate to God on the basis of what we do but on the basis of what Christ has done. Freedom from fear, because we have not been given a spirit of fear but of power, love, and a sound mind (2 Timothy 1:7). Freedom from shame, because the Spirit of adoption cries Abba Father in our hearts (Romans 8:15). Freedom from sin’s dominion, because sin shall not have mastery over us, since we are not under law but under grace (Romans 6:14).

And notice where the Spirit is. He is not in a building you have to reach. He is not in a state of mind you have to manufacture. He is in you. If you belong to Christ, the Spirit is in you. Which means freedom is in you. The freedom you are longing for is not a distant island you have to swim to. It is the awakening to what is already true in the room you are standing in.

This is not freedom to do whatever you want—the world tries to sell that and finds out too late it is just a new kind of slavery. This is freedom to be who you really are. A son. A daughter. A beloved one of God. Secure in the Father. Alive in Christ. Indwelt by the Spirit. That kind of freedom does not have to act out. It has nothing to prove. It is the rest of someone who knows whose she is.

So today, breathe. The chains the enemy keeps trying to convince you that you are still wearing have already been cut by the cross and the empty tomb. The Spirit who fell at Pentecost is the Spirit who lives in you, and where He is, freedom is. You may simply need to look down and notice the chains are already on the ground. Walk free.

Prayer

Father, thank You that Your Spirit and Your freedom are inseparable. Where He is, freedom is. Today, open my eyes to see the chains that have already been cut. Quiet every voice that argues against my liberty in Christ. Let me walk through this day not striving to become free, but awake to the freedom Your Spirit already brought into me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. The Spirit is in me. Therefore freedom is in me. I am not striving to become free. I am awake to the freedom that is already mine in Christ. The chains are on the ground. I walk free.
